issue.title: Document %queue capacity multipliers in xprompts memory
issue.description: Proposed by sase-19f.3 note #1. The approved epic plan explicitly deferred updating sase/memory/xprompts.md. Its %queue paragraph still states that capacity must be a positive integer, but %q(1.5x, w=0.25) now parses and resolves against effective max_running_agents. Update the table and paragraph with <M>x syntax, two-decimal precision, live effective-budget scaling, and the 1.5x * 5 = 7.5 example. Run sase memory init after the authorized edit. Distinct from sase-134, which documents %hold and proc queue behavior.

task_type_fields.proposed_change: Explain %q(1.5x) multiplier syntax and its effective max_running_agents resolution; replace integer-only guidance and regenerate memory output.

payload.entry: Documented %queue <M>x multipliers in sase/memory/xprompts.md: table row now shows capacity (N or <M>x); paragraph covers multiplier syntax, finite/>0/two-decimal rule with canonical trimmed formatting (1.50x reads as 1.5x), admission-time resolution against live effective max_running_agents rounded to two decimals, and the %q(1.5x, w=0.25) x effective-limit-5 = 7.5 budget example; integer-N fixed-budget semantics preserved. Verified: sase memory init --no-commit regenerated README stats (reference note, AGENTS.md unchanged), sase init memory --check passes, just fmt clean. Full just check could not complete in-turn: blocked by pre-existing workspace skew (installed sase-core-rs 0.34.71 vs linked checkout 0.34.73, needs just install rebuild); unrelated to this docs-only edit.
